questions.stem: Which of the following sterilization methods is best suited for heat-sensitive liquids?
questions.solutionHtml: Filtration is used for heat-sensitive liquids such as vaccines and antibiotics since it avoids thermal degradation.

questions.stem: Which bacterial structure is responsible for adherence to host surfaces?
questions.solutionHtml: Pili (Fimbriae) help bacteria adhere to surfaces and are important in pathogenesis.

questions.stem: Which bacterial species lacks a cell wall?
questions.solutionHtml: p>Explanation: Mycoplasma species lack a cell wall and instead have sterols in their membrane for structural stability.

questions.stem: Which of the following fungi is dimorphic?
questions.solutionHtml: Histoplasma exists as a mold at 25°C and a yeast at 37°C, characteristic of dimorphic fungi.

questions.stem: India ink staining is used to detect which fungal pathogen?
questions.solutionHtml: India ink staining highlights the polysaccharide capsule of Cryptococcus neoformans.

questions.stem: Which protozoan parasite causes steatorrhea?
questions.solutionHtml: Giardia causes steatorrhea and malabsorption by disrupting intestinal villi.

questions.stem: Which helminth is associated with rectal prolapse in heavy infections?
questions.solutionHtml: Heavy whipworm infections cause tenesmus, dysentery, and rectal prolapse.

questions.stem: The vector for Leishmania donovani is:
questions.solutionHtml: on: Sandflies (Phlebotomus species) transmit Leishmania donovani, causing visceral leishmaniasis.

questions.stem: Which DNA virus replicates in the cytoplasm?
questions.solutionHtml: on: Poxviruses have their own DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, allowing cytoplasmic replication.

questions.stem: Which hepatitis virus is a DNA virus?
questions.solutionHtml: n: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a partially double-stranded DNA virus.

questions.stem: Which of the following viruses does NOT establish latency?
questions.solutionHtml: on: Measles does not establish latency, while herpesviruses can remain dormant.

questions.stem: Which bacterial toxin inhibits protein synthesis by ADP-ribosylation of EF-2?
questions.solutionHtml: n: Diphtheria toxin inhibits elongation factor-2 (EF-2), stopping protein synthesis.

questions.stem: Which of the following bacteria is oxidase positive?
questions.solutionHtml: on: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is oxidase positive and produces a green pigment

questions.stem: Which bacterial infection is associated with rice-water stools?
questions.solutionHtml: on: Cholera toxin induces profuse, watery diarrhea, leading to rice-water stools.

questions.stem: Which bacterial structure is involved in biofilm formation?
questions.solutionHtml: ion: Exopolysaccharides aid in biofilm formation, providing bacterial protection from antibiotics and immune defenses

questions.stem: Which staining technique is used to detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis in sputum samples?
questions.solutionHtml: on: Mycobacterium tuberculosis contains mycolic acid in its cell wall, requiring an acid-fast stain for visualization

questions.stem: Which bacterial growth phase is characterized by the most rapid cell division?
questions.solutionHtml: on: In the log (exponential) phase, bacteria divide at their maximum rate.

questions.stem: Which hypersensitivity reaction is mediated by IgE?
questions.solutionHtml: tion: Type I hypersensitivity involves IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation, leading to allergic reactions.

questions.stem: What is the most common cause of fungal meningitis in AIDS patients?
questions.solutionHtml: on: Cryptococcus is an opportunistic fungus that causes meningitis in immunocompromised patients, including those with AIDS.

questions.stem: Which parasite causes vitamin B12 deficiency?
questions.solutionHtml: on: Diphyllobothrium latum competes for vitamin B12 in the intestine, leading to megaloblastic anemia.

questions.stem: Which of the following causes "winterbottom’s sign" (posterior cervical lymphadenopathy)?
questions.solutionHtml: on: Winterbottom’s sign is characteristic of African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness).

questions.stem: Which diagnostic test is preferred for detecting Toxoplasma gondii in neonates?
questions.solutionHtml: on: The Sabin-Feldman test is highly specific for Toxoplasma detection.

questions.stem: Which virus is detected by the Heterophile antibody test?
questions.solutionHtml: on: Heterophile antibodies are used to diagnose infectious mononucleosis caused by EBV.

questions.stem: Which of the following bacteria is NOT a facultative intracellular pathogen?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Streptococcus pyogenes

questions.stem: Which bacterium produces "safety pin" appearance on Wayson stain?
questions.solutionHtml: ion: Yersinia pestis exhibits bipolar staining, giving it a "safety pin" appearance.

questions.stem: Which bacterial species is most commonly associated with infective endocarditis in IV drug users?
questions.solutionHtml: ion: S. aureus is the leading cause of endocarditis in IV drug users, often affecting the tricuspid valve.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an obligate anaerobe?
questions.solutionHtml: n: Obligate anaerobes, like Clostridium species, cannot survive in oxygen-rich environments.

questions.stem: Which type of culture media is used for the isolation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis?
questions.solutionHtml: n: Lowenstein-Jensen medium is selective for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of Type IV hypersensitivity?
questions.solutionHtml: n: Type IV hypersensitivity is delayed and mediated by T cells (e.g., tuberculin reaction).

questions.stem: Which of the following fungi is associated with "spaghetti and meatballs" appearance on KOH mount?
questions.solutionHtml: tion: Malassezia furfur causes tinea versicolor and exhibits "spaghetti and meatballs" appearance on KOH prep.

questions.stem: Which systemic mycosis is causes Darling’s disease?
questions.solutionHtml: tion: Histoplasmosis is prevalent in soil contaminated with bird and bat droppings in these regions. It causes Darling’s disease

questions.stem: Which of the following is the diagnostic stage for Plasmodium falciparum?
questions.solutionHtml: on: The crescent-shaped gametocyte is the diagnostic stage of Plasmodium falciparum.

questions.stem: Which parasite causes Kala-azar?
questions.solutionHtml: tion: Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) is caused by Leishmania donovani and transmitted by sandflies.

questions.stem: Which virus is associated with subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE)?
questions.solutionHtml: ion: SSPE is a late neurological complication of measles.

questions.stem: Which bacterial toxin blocks the release of acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction?
questions.solutionHtml: ion: Botulinum toxin causes flaccid paralysis by preventing acetylcholine release.

questions.stem: Which bacteria are known for producing sulfur granules in infections?
questions.solutionHtml: ion: Actinomyces causes chronic abscesses with sulfur granules, often in cervicofacial infections.

questions.stem: Which bacterial species is commonly associated with "flesh-eating" disease (necrotizing fasciitis)?
questions.solutionHtml: tion: S. pyogenes releases exotoxins that contribute to tissue destruction in necrotizing fasciitis.

questions.stem: Which antiviral drug inhibits neuraminidase activity in influenza?
questions.solutionHtml: on: Oseltamivir (Tamiflu) prevents viral release by inhibiting neuraminidase.

questions.stem: Which viral infection is most commonly linked to congenital abnormalities?
questions.solutionHtml: tion: Congenital CMV infection causes sensorineural deafness, microcephaly, and hepatosplenomegaly.

questions.stem: Which fungal infection is most commonly associated with neutropenic patients?
questions.solutionHtml: on: Invasive aspergillosis is a significant concern in neutropenic patients.
